causes.text: In mid-February 2024, U.S. natural gas producers including Antero Resources, Comstock Resources and EQT Corp said they would cut capital spending and reduce drilling after prices plunged, dropping rigs and delaying wells to prioritize free cash flow.

source_info.title: US natgas drillers cut spending, reduce activity amid price crash

effects.text: On its April 2024 results day, Halliburton said it expects North American revenue to remain flat for 2024 amid weak U.S. drilling demand, while forecasting low double-digit growth internationally.

source_info.title: Halliburton beats quarterly profit estimates on growing international strength; North America seen flat

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Major U.S. gas producers announced budget and activity cuts (rig drops, deferred wells) after prices hit multi-year lows, signaling a contraction in U.S. gas-weighted drilling demand.
Oilfield services demand in North America is tightly linked to E&P capex. When producers pull back, service activity and pricing are pressured.
Halliburton guided that 2024 North American revenue would be flat year-on-year, while international growth would offset weakness driven by low U.S. gas prices.
Shares were modestly lower on the day (about −0.3% close-to-close), reflecting muted sentiment toward the North American outlook.

rationale: Producers' capex cuts are a leading indicator for oilfield-service activity. The February 2024 pullback among gas-weighted E&Ps set expectations for weaker U.S. drilling demand, which Halliburton echoed by guiding North America to flat revenues for 2024.
counterfactual_analysis: If U.S. gas prices had held up and producers maintained drilling budgets, Halliburton likely would have projected growth rather than flat North American revenues, and the stock reaction could have been positive.

adversarial_confounders.text: Halliburton's North American guide might also reflect firm-specific factors (e.g., equipment mix, pricing strategy) or supply constraints unrelated to E&P budgets.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Would weaken the extent to which producer cuts alone explain the flat outlook.

adversarial_confounders.text: Policy or regulatory developments (permits, emissions rules) could dampen activity independently of commodity prices.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Could reduce North American service demand even if producers' capex decisions were unchanged.

details.commentary: Gas producers' decision to cut drilling and defer wells reduced the volume of work available to North American service companies. With fewer jobs to bid on, Halliburton faced a tougher fight for contracts and less leverage to sustain pricing in its core market.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - U.S. natural gas price slump
details.commentary: A slump in U.S. natural gas prices squeezed cash flows at gas-focused E&Ps, forcing them to retrench on capital spending. These economic conditions directly translated into weaker rig activity and a softer demand outlook for Halliburton's North American operations.

Lower gas prices prompted capex cuts that reduced service activity, which in turn pressured Halliburton's revenue and made management more cautious in its outlook. That balancing loop kept North American revenue expectations flat even as the company leaned more heavily on stronger international markets for growth.
